units.source: Go is easier to learn when the explanations are accessible in your language. This community project localizes Go learning resources and documentation while keeping the canonical Go content as its reference.

Explore the interactive lessons and runnable examples in ⟦P0⟧A Tour of Go⟦P1⟧, learning resources, and practical Go documentation. The project also localizes navigation, project information, and other shared site content. Future Go content can be added through the same translation and review process.

The localized collection contains 156 independent Go content pages: the Go homepage, 104 pages in A Tour of Go, and 51 Learn and Docs pages. These counts describe this project's translated collection, not every page on ⟦P0⟧. Availability can differ by language.
1 page. An introduction to Go and a starting point for exploring the language.
1 page. Find resources for getting started and building your Go skills.
104 pages. Explore interactive lessons and runnable examples covering language basics, methods, interfaces, and concurrency.
1 page. Find your way around Go's documentation and its main topics.
1 page. Download and install Go on your system.
18 pages. Follow practical guides to writing Go programs, using modules, working with data, testing, and finding vulnerabilities.
9 pages. Learn to open database connections, query and change data, manage transactions, and cancel operations.
9 pages. Develop modules, manage dependencies, organize source code, and publish releases.
12 pages. Read about secure development, security policy, fuzzing, and vulnerability management.

The Tour count includes 103 lesson pages and one independent contents page. Its entry route is not counted as an additional content page. This project-owned About page is not part of the 156-page total.

The canonical Tour's Go local directory includes four links to this project's language editions. Four additional live language editions have been submitted for inclusion in Go local through ⟦P0⟧golang/go#81958⟦P1⟧. The issue remains open; these applications have not been accepted or merged.
Work starts from the canonical Go source and a shared glossary for the language.
Language models assist with generating translations from those inputs.
Machine checks validate structure and protected details such as code, identifiers, and link targets.
A separate language review checks meaning, clarity, and terminology. Findings return for focused revision and another review.
Accepted content is checked together across the site, then goes through preview, maintainer checks, and release verification before publication.

Generating a translation and reviewing it are separate roles. The Reviewer does not write a replacement and then approve it; findings go back to the translation stage. Machine validation protects technical details, but it does not establish language quality. AI output is not published directly.

Revisions address the reported problem and matching instances within its scope. Another review checks that the problem has been resolved. These checks reduce mistakes, but translations can still contain errors, and reports from readers help improve them.
Each language uses one glossary across all surfaces. Source changes and reviewed glossary changes reopen only the affected content, with verified evidence for reuse of unaffected work.

Translations follow a recorded version of the canonical source. Updates to that source are checked to identify the content that needs attention. Changed content returns through the necessary translation and review steps; accepted unchanged work can be retained. The project is maintained over time.

Translations may differ from the latest official English website. Unavailable local pages link directly to the official source; direct requests to missing local pages return a real not-found response.

Report translation problems through the issue tracker, including the language, page, and relevant text. The repository contains the project source and development history; it is also the place to discuss contributions.

slots.text: 如果能以自己的语言阅读说明，学习 Go 会更加轻松。本社区项目对 Go 学习资源和文档进行本地化，并以 Go 的规范源内容作为参考。
包含哪些内容
探索⟦P0⟧Go 语言之旅⟦P1⟧中的交互式课程和可运行示例、学习资源以及实用的 Go 文档。本项目还会本地化导航、项目信息和其他共享站点内容。未来的 Go 内容也可以通过同一套翻译与审核流程加入。
已翻译的 156 个 Go 页面
本地化内容集合包含 156 个独立的 Go 内容页面：Go 首页、Go 语言之旅中的 104 个页面，以及 51 个学习与文档页面。这些数量描述的是本项目的翻译内容集合，而不是⟦P0⟧上的所有页面。不同语言的可用内容可能有所不同。

翻译如何生成
工作从 Go 的规范源内容以及该语言统一使用的术语表开始。
语言模型根据这些输入协助生成翻译。
机器检查验证结构和受保护的细节，例如代码、标识符和链接目标。
独立的语言审核检查语义、清晰度和术语。发现的问题会返回进行针对性修订，并再次审核。
通过审核的内容会在整个站点范围内进行整体检查，然后经过预览、维护者检查和发布验证后再发布。
质量与独立审核
翻译生成与审核由不同角色承担。审核者不会先写出替换译文再自行批准；发现的问题会返回翻译阶段。机器验证会保护技术细节，但不能证明语言质量。AI 输出不会直接发布。
修订会处理已报告的问题，以及其范围内的同类实例。之后由另一轮审核确认问题是否已经解决。这些检查能减少错误，但翻译仍可能存在问题，读者反馈有助于持续改进。
持续维护
翻译以已记录的规范源版本为准。规范源更新时，会检查哪些内容需要处理。发生变化的内容会重新经过必要的翻译和审核步骤；已接受且未变化的成果可以保留。项目会持续维护。
反馈与项目源代码
通过问题跟踪系统报告翻译问题，并注明语言、页面和相关文本。代码仓库包含项目源代码和开发历史，也可用于讨论贡献。
支持 ⟦P0⟧ 运营成本
非官方社区项目
这是一个非官方的社区本地化项目。Go 的规范源内容仍是权威依据。本项目不声称与 Go 项目存在隶属关系或获得其认可。
